body:
### Problem

Most work in a GitHub-hosted repo starts life as a GitHub issue, but vincent knows nothing about GitHub. Creating a task for an existing issue means opening the issue in a browser, copying the title into the new-task form, copying the body into the description, and then re-typing anything the workflow needs as a declared field. The issue number and URL survive only if the human remembers to paste them, and the agent that eventually runs the workflow never sees the issue's labels, author or link at all — a workflow prompt cannot say "fix the bug described below" because there is nothing in the §8.4 template context to interpolate.

Today there is no GitHub concept anywhere in the tree: `store.Project` has no remote or host field, `config.yaml` has no `github` key, and `workflow.RenderContext` has no issue surface.

### Proposed solution

When a project is GitHub-based **and** GitHub integration is enabled, let the human pick a GitHub issue while creating a task. The pick prefills the task and is carried into the workflow's template context so issue details are available to prompts and commands.

This is the first piece of a broader GitHub integration; **checking on pull requests is the intended next piece** and should not be designed out, but it is explicitly not in scope here.

**Detection and enablement.** "GitHub-based" is derived, not stored: parse the project's `origin` remote for a github.com host at the point of use. No new `Project` column and no migration. "Enabled" is a `config.yaml` toggle, so a user who does not want the daemon reading GitHub can turn it off; hot reload applies as it does for the rest of config.

**Authentication.** Prefer the `gh` CLI (`gh issue list/view --json …`) and fall back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` from the daemon's inherited environment when `gh` is absent or unauthenticated. vincent stores no credential of its own, which keeps spec §2's "secret management" non-goal intact and matches how the daemon already drives external CLIs. The daemon makes the call — clients never talk to GitHub, per the ownership invariant. `gitx.RemoteTimeout` is the precedent for bounding it.

**Surfaces.**

- TUI: an issue row in the new-task form, opening a picker in the same shape as the existing project/workflow/agent pickers (`internal/tui/newtaskpicker.go`). Default listing is open issues, newest first, narrowable by typed text; the row belongs in the §15 form order, before title.
- API: a `github_issue` field on `POST /v1/tasks`, plus whatever read endpoint the picker needs to list issues for a project. The TUI holds no state the daemon doesn't have, so this exists regardless of the TUI.
- CLI: `vincent task create --github-issue 123`, resolved daemon-side, with explicit flags winning over anything the issue would have prefilled; and a list command (`vincent github issues`) so issues can be browsed without opening the TUI.

**What the pick fills in.** Title from the issue title, description from the issue body, a link line carrying the issue number and URL appended to the description so a task read on its own still points back, and a best-effort mapping of issue metadata (labels, assignee, milestone) onto the workflow's declared `fields:` (§8.1.2) where the names line up. Everything lands in the form's editable rows — nothing is locked, and a human can rewrite or clear any of it before creating. Because the mapping guesses, it must be visible in the form before creation rather than applied silently at run time.

**Template context.** A new top-level `.Issue` in `workflow.RenderContext` (number, title, body, URL, state, labels, author, …), zero-valued when no issue is linked so a template shared between linked and unlinked tasks can test it — the same convention `.Loop`'s `Index: 0` already uses. Rendering must stay a pure, offline operation.

**Freshness.** The issue is fetched once at task creation and persisted on the task; every step renders from that snapshot. This is the same reasoning that makes vincent snapshot the workflow YAML at creation: a run is reproducible, no network call enters the step path, and a step render still cannot fail for an external reason. An issue edited on GitHub after task creation is deliberately not reflected.

**When GitHub is unavailable** — `gh` missing, not authenticated, no token, rate-limited, offline — the issue row is not offered and the daemon logs the concrete reason. In addition, `vincent doctor` gains a row reporting `gh` presence and authentication state, so the diagnosis lives beside the other environment checks rather than only in the daemon log.

**Acceptance criteria**

- With integration enabled and a GitHub `origin`, the TUI new-task form offers an issue picker; selecting an issue fills title, description, link line and matching declared fields, and every one of them is still editable.
- With integration disabled, or on a project whose `origin` is not GitHub, no issue row appears and no GitHub call is made.
- A task created from issue N renders `.Issue.Number`, `.Issue.Title`, `.Issue.Body`, `.Issue.URL` and `.Issue.Labels` in an agent or command step; a task created without one renders the zero value and a `{{ if .Issue.Number }}` template works on both.
- `vincent task create --github-issue N` produces the same stored task as the TUI path; explicit flags override the issue-derived values.
- `vincent github issues` lists selectable issues for a project.
- Editing the issue on GitHub after creation does not change what a later step renders.
- With `gh` absent and no token set: no issue row, a logged reason, and a `vincent doctor` row saying so — task creation without an issue is unaffected.
- Cross-platform: the `gh` invocation and the token fallback both work on Windows, macOS and Linux.

### Alternatives considered

- **Store the GitHub repo on `Project`** (`github_repo: owner/name`, auto-filled at registration, editable). Handles SSH aliases and non-`origin` GitHub remotes, and would let the projects view show the link — but it costs a migration and a new editable field for a fact that is derivable today. Worth revisiting if remote parsing proves too narrow, or when PR checking lands and needs a durable repo identity.
- **Flatten issue data into `Task.Fields`** as `github_issue_number`, `github_issue_body`, … instead of a `.Issue` struct. No new context type and it works in every existing template, but it collides with user-declared field names and flattens labels into a joined string.
- **Store a GitHub token in `config.yaml`.** Self-contained and independent of `gh`, but it makes vincent a secret store, which spec §2 declines.
- **Re-fetch the issue on every step render.** Always current, at the cost of a network call and a new failure mode inside rendering, which today cannot fail for external reasons.
- **Prefill the title only** and leave the body reachable solely through `.Issue.Body`. Keeps the description for the human's own framing, but loses the at-a-glance context on the board and in the detail view.

### Spec reference

§5.1 (Project), §5.3 (Task), §8.1.2 (declared task fields), §8.4 (template context), §13.2 (endpoints), §15 (TUI new-task form). §2 non-goal "secret management (daemon inherits the user's environment)" is what selects the `gh`/env-token approach. Decision record row 11 — "Delivery owned entirely by workflow steps; no hardcoded push/PR/merge behavior" — is not contradicted by this: reading an issue to prefill a task is input, not delivery, and no push, PR or merge behavior is added. That row does become live when PR checking arrives, so the design should keep GitHub access out of the delivery path.
title: GitHub integration: select a GitHub issue when creating a task
